newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Seven groups bid for Manila power project.
newsitem.headline: Seven groups bid for Manila power project.

text.p: Seven local and foreign groups submitted bids on Monday to the National Power Corp (Napocor) for the construction of a 1,200-megawatt gas-fired power plant, Napocor officials said.

The groups were Marubeni Corp of Japan with Sithe Energy, Korea Electric Power Co, AES Transpower of the U.S. in joint venture with Aboitiz Equity Ventures and Nichimen Corp, Alsons Power Holdings with Tomen Corp and Singapore Power Inc., PowerGen International with Siemens AG, Ilijan Power Corp led by Enron Corp and Consolidated Electric Power Asia Ltd with Mitsubishi Corp.
Napocor officials, who opened the technical bids of the seven groups, said the financial bids will be opened at a later date.
The officials said the financial bids may be opened in December, earlier than the original January 3 schedule, as only seven companies had submitted tenders.
Some 20 local and foreign companies had bought Napocor's bidding documents.
Contract signing is slated on September 30, 1997. The power plant is scheduled to be ready for commercial operation on January 2, 2002.

Monday's bids were part of a rebidding ordered by the state-owned Napocor after it last year threw out the bid of Consolidated Electric Power Asia Ltd and its partner Mitsubishi, even though it was the lowest.
It said the action was taken because the group would be using technology developed by Mitsubishi and Westinghouse.

The Philippine government had banned Westinghouse from all local power projects due to a conflict over a nuclear power plant in Bataan in the northern Philippines, although it has since reached a settlement with Westinghouse.
Napocor had insisted there should be a new bid even though it had lifted the ban on Westinghouse products.
